body:
THE DIVISION PLAN YOU ASKED FOR, with criterion 1 already implemented and up as PR #2045 so you are checking something concrete rather than a proposal.

YOUR OWNERSHIP RULING SHAPED THE SPLIT AND I THINK IT IS RIGHT. "Anything that reads or writes the format is one piece regardless of how many criteria it spans" is the line I cut on.

PIECE 1 — THE FORMAT. DONE, PR #2045, one owner, not divisible.

  `rounds` as an append-only array; the current round stays at the top level so
  read_recorded_verdict, the drain's arming path and the merge gate are untouched.
  Round identity = the head REVIEWED. `findings_surviving_round(body) -> Vec<String>`
  compares against the PREVIOUS round only.

  This is criterion 1 plus the seam BUG-1505's criteria 7 and 10 consume. It is the
  piece you said must stay with one owner, and it is closed.

PIECE 2 — SURFACING (criteria 2 and 3). Divisible, depends on piece 1's seam only.

  Call findings_surviving_round at verdict-record time; put survivors on the spec and in
  the rework prompt. Two workers could split "on the spec" from "in the prompt" without
  touching the format.

  CRITERION 3 IS THE RISKY HALF AND IT IS NOT A FORMAT PROBLEM. The spec is explicit that
  the signal must read as "check whether this is implementable as written", NOT as an
  implementer-performance signal — because the performance framing produces exactly the
  escalating firmness that failed three times. That is a wording judgment, it is the whole
  point of the spec, and I would not hand it to a headless implementer.

PIECE 3 — BUG-1505 criteria 7 and 10. Blocked on piece 1, which is now unblocked.

TWO THINGS I FOUND WHILE IMPLEMENTING THAT BEAR ON HOW YOU DIVIDE THE REST:

1. THE SPEC'S OWN FAILURE MODE NEARLY ARRIVED THROUGH ITS IMPLEMENTATION, twice. I first
   keyed round identity on reviewed_sha PLUS recorded_at — but record_verdict stamps
   recorded_at on every call, so every re-record looked like a new round. Then my dedup
   checked whether a snapshot was already IN rounds, which always passes when rounds is
   empty. Either bug makes a round its own predecessor, so EVERY finding reads as
   surviving — the signal built to prevent escalating firmness becomes a generator of it.

   Both were caught by tests, not by me. This is the concrete form of what you refused to
   leave undecided.

2. MY FALSIFIABILITY PASS FOUND A HOLE IN MY OWN TESTS. Breaking the comparison to use the
   FIRST round instead of the previous one changed behaviour and nothing went red — every
   test built exactly two rounds, where first and last are the same object. Same vacuous-
   coverage shape the reviewer has been finding all night, in my work. Fixed with a
   three-round regression fixture; the full matrix is in the PR body.

ON YOUR THREE OPERATIONAL FACTS: branch confirmed — I created story-1391-verdict-rounds off
a553d7e927 before your mail arrived, so we converged independently. I did NOT touch
story-1391-work. The flag-only in-progress lease is still unreconciled and I have not touched
that either; it is disposition and it is the BUG-1510 instance you named.
